app.name: Parley
app.oneLiner: Floating-orb voice dictation and voice edit for any Android text field.
app.problem: Typing on a phone is slow and error-prone, and the built-in voice typing lives inside one keyboard, gets names wrong, and cannot rewrite what is already written. The Mac version of Parley fixed this with a system-wide gesture: tap-tap-hold, speak, release, and the text lands at the cursor, or say 'make it shorter' and the field is rewritten. On Android there is no equivalent that works in every app without replacing the keyboard.
app.targetUsers: One person: the author of Parley for macOS, dictating into chat, mail and notes apps on their own Android phone, with their own Groq and MiniMax API keys.
nonGoals: A keyboard (IME). The orb sits over whatever keyboard is already installed.
Google Play distribution. Personal use, sideloaded with adb, so no Play accessibility-policy work.
iOS. iOS has no API for an overlay that inserts text into other apps; the ios/ folder stays untouched.
Sync with the Mac app. The phone stands alone in v1.

in: Floating orb over every app, drawn by an accessibility overlay: hold it to dictate, release to insert
Volume-down tap-tap-hold as a second trigger, mirroring the Mac gesture
Dictation: Groq Whisper transcribes and the text is inserted at the cursor of the focused field
Voice edit: double-tap then hold the orb (orb-only in v1) and speak an instruction; MiniMax rewrites the selection or the whole field
History of dictations and edits, with the time saved on an Overview
First-run setup: API keys, microphone, accessibility service, battery exemption, one practice dictation
out: Personal dictionary (names and jargon) — v1.1, same Whisper-prompt approach as desktop
Explain-selection popover — v1.1, via the text-selection PROCESS_TEXT menu
Dictionary or history sync with the Mac app
Play Store release and its prominent-disclosure flow

decisions.question: How does it ship — Play Store, sideload for others, or personal use?
decisions.answer: Personal use only. Sideloaded debug/release APK on the author's phone.

decisions.question: What starts a recording?
decisions.answer: Both: hold the floating orb, or triple-press volume-down holding the third press.

decisions.question: What is in v1?
decisions.answer: Dictation, voice edit, and history with time saved. Personal dictionary is not in v1.

decisions.question: Does the phone share data with the Mac app?
Which rocketship scaffolder?
decisions.answer: create-flutter-app. It is the mobile scaffolder with the full 13/13 harness and planning skills; create-react-native-app ships without the harness docs.
decisions.why: The user asked to use rocketship and to pick the boilerplate; Flutter is the only mobile one with the full harness

decisions.question: Where does the dictation pipeline run — Dart or Kotlin?
decisions.answer: Kotlin, inside the accessibility service process. Flutter owns only the app screens and talks to the service over one MethodChannel + one EventChannel.
decisions.why: The pipeline must run while the Flutter UI is closed; a headless Flutter engine per recording adds 30-40 MB and start-up latency to the one path that has to feel instant

decisions.question: How is the orb drawn?
decisions.answer: A native Kotlin Canvas view in a TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY window, not a Flutter view.
decisions.why: The accessibility overlay type needs no SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW permission, and a native view animates mic levels without keeping a second Flutter engine alive

decisions.question: Who owns history and settings storage?
decisions.answer: The native side. SQLite for history, EncryptedSharedPreferences for keys and settings. Flutter reads and writes only through the bridge.
decisions.why: One writer, no sync: the service writes history while the app is closed, and two stores (Drift + native) would drift

decisions.question: How is text inserted into another app's field?
decisions.answer: ACTION_SET_TEXT on the focused editable node, splicing at the selection; fallback is clipboard + ACTION_PASTE; last resort is clipboard + a 'copied' state on the orb.
decisions.why: SET_TEXT keeps the clipboard untouched and works in native and Compose fields; Chrome web fields and some custom editors only accept paste

decisions.question: How much should the look matter?
decisions.answer: A lot: the UI should look amazing, with a very good theme.

decisions.question: Which visual identity?
decisions.answer: Aurora: dark-first ink ground, the Mac app's indigo/amber/green mode colours, Instrument Serif + Geist + Geist Mono, the orb as the only glow.
decisions.why: Carries the Mac orb palette over so both apps read as one product, and a serif for the user's own words sets transcripts apart from interface text

navigation.ascii:
First run
  └─ /setup              Setup (sequence, no tab) → /
Home shell
  ├─ /                   Overview (tab 1)
  ├─ /history            History (tab 2)
  ├─ /history/:id        Transcript (pushed from row)
  ├─ /settings           Settings (tab 3)
  └─ /settings/keys      API keys (pushed from Settings)
Outside Flutter (native)
  └─ Orb overlay + accessibility service, running over every app

tokens: Identity name: aurora (docs/design/aurora.md), swapped in for the shipped halo identity through lib/theme/spec; palette-lint K1..K7 must pass in both themes
Dark is the default theme; light is fully supported. Dark: ground #0E0E14, surface #17171F, raised #1F1F2A, border #23232F, text #EDEDF5, muted #9C9CB2, action fill #5555E0, action text #8B8BFF
Light: ground #F5F5F8, surface #FFFFFF, raised #EFEFF5, border #E6E6EE, text #15151D, muted #5C5C70, action #4646D6

Mode colours shared by orb, status dots and history dots: dictation #8B8BFF (indigo, hue 277 as on the Mac), voice edit #F4B942 (amber), inserted #4CD38A (green), error #FF6E6E. Light-mode text variants darken to pass 4.5:1

Typefaces: Instrument Serif for titles and for the user's own words (transcripts, instructions, italic in quotes); Geist for interface text; Geist Mono for figures. Four sizes: 40 / 22 / 16 / 13, plus 32 mono for stats
Shape: cards 24 radius (hero 28), buttons 18, chips pill. 8-point spacing. Borders instead of shadows in dark; soft tinted shadows in light

The orb is the only glow in the app: layered radial gradient in the mode colour, breathing 4.2 s when idle, 1.1 s pulse plus expanding ring while listening, spinning arc while working. No gradient washes on backgrounds
Motion: 200 ms cross-fades, springy orb state changes, respects reduce-motion (orb stops breathing, keeps colour)

openQuestions: Android 14+ restricts starting a microphone foreground service from the background. Does a bound accessibility service with a visible accessibility overlay qualify for the while-in-use exemption on the author's phone? Spike parley-a01 answers this before anything else is built.

Consuming volume-down to detect tap-tap-hold means single presses must be replayed as volume changes after the gesture window (~350 ms). Is that lag acceptable, or should the gesture be volume-down + volume-up chord instead?
Which apps reject ACTION_SET_TEXT? Chrome and WebView fields are expected to need the paste fallback; the spike logs the insert method per app.
